items.title: NHS savings drive leaves hospitals in England facing ‘unpalatable’ cuts
items.desc: Exclusive: Thirty-one trusts issue stark warning that cost-cutting demands threaten their ability to function normally Dozens of hospitals are so short of money they may not be able to continue caring for patients and are being forced to make “unpalatable” cuts to services and staff, the Guardian can reveal. Thirty-one health service trusts in England have issued stark warnings that NHS demands for them to make huge budget savings this year threaten their ability to function normally. All have declared that as a threat in the register of risks they have to maintain and publish. Continue reading...

items.title: Russell Brand’s wife vows to abide by prison rules after video controversy
items.desc: Laura Brand says in new video on YouTube she will continue Sunday Service series she started with Brand Russell Brand’s wife, Laura, has promised to “absolutely honour” rules set by the prison where her convicted sex offender husband is being held, in another YouTube video published on Sunday. This week Andy Burnham called on Google to take down a video uploaded to Russell Brand’s YouTube channel last Sunday that contained a statement from the disgraced comedian in prison, where he is serving a 10-and-a-half-year sentence for rape and sexual assaults. items.title: Pip review will call for overhaul rather than scrapping benefit for under-25s
items.desc: Recommendations overseen by Stephen Timms would retain system for all ages, unlike last week’s Milburn review A long-awaited review of the personal independence payment (Pip) system will this week recommend that it is overhauled, a week after another report called for it to be partly scrapped. The final report on Pip by a committee co-led by Stephen Timms, the social security minister, is expected to be published as soon as Tuesday, presenting Andy Burnham with one of his most politically sensitive decisions yet as prime minister. Continue reading...

items.title: Theresa May’s blast from the past calls Tories back to their unhappy place | Peter Walker
items.desc: Conservatives may instinctively want to push back against closer EU ties, but they have to train their focus elsewhere Anyone who accidentally switched to BBC One at about 9.45am on Sunday to be greeted by Theresa May awkwardly espousing the virtues of Brexit could have been forgiven for thinking they had woken up in around 2018 – and not being especially pleased at the idea. This is one of the problems now facing May’s party. For all that it is a reflex action for Conservatives to push back against closer ties with the EU, Andy Burnham’s decision to pursue such a course plunges them back into their own unhappy place. Continue reading...

items.title: UK taxpayers held more than £1tn in offshore tax havens, latest HMRC data shows
items.desc: Figures show recent 10% rise in total held in financial centres such as Jersey and Panama, raising fears over cost to public purse The amount of money UK taxpayers hold in offshore accounts in tax havens has exceeded £1tn for the first time, raising concerns about potential losses to the public purse. HM Revenue and Customs (HMRC) data, obtained by the TaxWatch thinktank through freedom of information requests, shows between 2022 and 2024 the value of balances held offshore in tax havens increased by 10%. These were the latest available figures. Continue reading...

The bestselling author’s fifth romance series novel, Prudence, published in 1978, allegedly includes several plagiarised passages from The Serial by Cyra McFadden and The Franchise Affair by Josephine Tey. items.title: Man who killed three during psychotic episode ‘had been released after catalogue of failures’
items.desc: Alexander Lewis-Ranwell was arrested and let go twice by police in the 48 hours before he killed three men in their 80s in Exeter A man with paranoid schizophrenia who killed three people while experiencing a psychotic episode had been released from custody after a “catalogue of failures” by police and medical professionals, an investigation has found. Alexander Lewis-Ranwell was arrested and released twice by police in the 48 hours before he killed Anthony Payne, 80, and the twin brothers Roger and Dick Carter, 84, in their homes in Exeter in 2019. items.title: CEO of funding agency for UK science and research criticised by union over cuts

The letter from Mike Clancy, the general secretary of Prospect, to Ian Chapman, the chief executive of UK Research and Innovation (UKRI), is the latest development in a row over changes in funding for projects and research facilities. items.title: Closer EU ties will give UK say on Brussels decisions, says Ed Miliband
items.desc: Foreign secretary says there is clear case to integrate more closely but does not say if he backs talks on possibly rejoining Closer links with the EU will mean the UK having a say on decisions made by Brussels, Ed Miliband has argued as ministers faced pressure to move further after Friday’s landmark deal with the EU. Any timetable for closer integration, including possible talks about the UK rejoining the EU, remains unclear after the Brussels summit, with Andy Burnham saying he would now “brainstorm” over future ties. items.title: Theresa May ‘aghast’ at Andy Burnham’s talk about rejoining EU
items.desc: Former PM who opted for minimal ties with bloc says moves towards membership would dominate government’s time Theresa May has said she feels “aghast” at Andy Burnham’s plan for potentially rejoining the EU, arguing in a rare interview that the prime minister should “accept Brexit and move on”. Speaking to the BBC after Friday’s UK-EU summit , at which Burnham secured the biggest step towards renewed ties with Brussels since Brexit, May said that a further move towards membership, as talked about by the PM, would dominate the government’s time. Continue reading...

items.title: UK-EU food deal hailed by British firms: ‘We’re pretty aligned anyway’
items.desc: Exporters welcome end in sight for Brexit checks – but are frustrated that implementation will take so long British producers have broadly welcomed the UK’s deal with the EU, designed to remove the vast majority of physical checks on food, plants and animal products. The sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) deal is expected to benefit Britain’s food exporters and will enable UK delicatessens and other small retailers to import European cheese and wine again, something that became economically unviable because of costly Brexit checks. Continue reading...

items.title: Exquisitely decorated home of Victorian workman David Parr wins blue plaque
items.desc: Working-class man who covered mansions with William Morris’s patterns spent his nights filling his Cambridge terrace house with his own designs As a Victorian working-class labourer, David Parr was paid to spend his days decorating the interiors of private mansions and Cambridge colleges with William Morris’s magnificent designs. But as an artist, Parr chose to spend his nights filling his modest terrace house with the most resplendent decor and exquisite craftsmanship he could create. Continue reading...

items.title: Hacks, AI and conspiracy theories: why are we having so many outages?
items.desc: After chaos at airlines, banks and companies from Microsoft to Apple, people have become convinced the world’s systems are under attack Nicole Reindorf’s American Airlines flight was ready for takeoff in Phoenix when the pilot came on the intercom and announced what was to become the longest nationwide aviation shutdown since 9/11 . Reindorf, 70, had seen the headlines hours before about a global Microsoft outage . She immediately suspected the two were linked in some way by AI-related threats – and that she would not get to the wedding of her best friend’s son in California. Continue reading...
